heading: Window controls need permission
body: client/manifest.json declares the window that a native target opens and the controls that a service may use, under `tac.application.window.controls`. By default, the manifest grants nothing. A service gets the controls by injection, like the other browser APIs: `@Needs windowControls` in JavaScript and TypeScript, and a `WindowControls` field in every language that runs in the page. Lua and Python services do not get `WindowControls`. A service that the native app links in has no page, but it can still get the controls: a Swift or Rust service in a macOS app, a C# service on Windows and a Kotlin service on Android declare an uninitialized `WindowControls` field with `Needs` or `NeedsAll`, and Tachyon calls the host directly, with the same grants (ADR 0089). A service never reads `globalThis` (`TY1360`). `granted(control)` answers whether a control is granted; ask it before you offer a control. A call to a control that is not granted fails at once, and the message names the grant to add. In a browser tab nothing is granted, because the page has no native window. The host checks the manifest grants again before it runs a request. A test unit fakes the controls like any browser API: a `@Fake windowControls` field in JavaScript and TypeScript, and `BrowserFakes` in Go, Ruby, Swift, C# and F#. These controls do not sandbox (restrict) the native service code that the application owns. That code runs with the operating system permissions of the host process. See the feature "What a page may do to its window" for the service in every language.
